questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a principle of Agile methodology?
o: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Responding to change over following a plan
questions.e: Agile values working software over comprehensive documentation, so preferring documentation is the opposite of an Agile principle.

questions.q: In software testing, what is the purpose of boundary value analysis?
o: To ensure security vulnerabilities are detected
To test values at the edges of input ranges
To verify data integrity in databases
To check system performance under load
questions.e: Boundary value analysis tests the smallest and largest valid values and the values just outside them, where bugs often hide.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a software design pattern?
o: To provide reusable solutions to common problems
questions.e: A design pattern is a proven, reusable solution to a common design problem.

questions.q: What is the key characteristic of DevOps in software development?
questions.e: DevOps joins development and operations with continuous integration and continuous delivery.

questions.q: In software development, what is the purpose of unit testing?
o: To test performance under high load
To test individual components in isolation
questions.e: Unit testing checks one small component, such as a function, on its own.

questions.q: Which software development methodology focuses on delivering small, functional increments frequently?
questions.e: Agile delivers small, working increments often.

questions.q: What is the role of an API Gateway in microservices architecture?
questions.e: An API gateway is the single entry point that routes and manages requests between clients and services.

questions.q: Which software development life cycle (SDLC) phase involves feasibility studies and requirement gathering?
questions.e: Planning is where feasibility is studied and requirements are gathered.

questions.q: In software engineering, which model is best suited for projects with rapidly changing requirements?
questions.e: Agile welcomes changing requirements because it works in short cycles.

questions.q: Which principle is essential for writing maintainable software?
questions.e: KISS says to keep designs simple, which makes software easier to maintain.

questions.q: Which design pattern ensures only one instance of a class is created?
questions.e: The Singleton pattern allows only one instance of a class.

questions.q: What does "agile" emphasize in software development?
questions.e: Agile means working in short, repeated cycles that deliver a little at a time.

questions.q: What does REST stand for in web services?
questions.e: REST stands for Representational State Transfer.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of microservices architecture?
questions.e: Microservices are small, independently deployed services, so one monolithic deployment is not a feature of them.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the Agile software development methodology?
questions.e: Agile prefers working software over heavy documentation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the "KISS" principle in software design?
questions.e: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Singleton design pattern?
o: To create a factory for object creation
To allow multiple instances of a class
To provide an interface for creating objects
To ensure only one instance of a class is created
questions.e: The Singleton pattern allows only one instance of a class.

questions.q: What does the term "API" stand for in the context of software development?
questions.e: API stands for Application Programming Interface.

questions.q: Which programming paradigm emphasizes the use of functions as the primary building blocks of software?
questions.e: Functional programming is built from functions.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the command "git pull" in version control systems?
o: Upload changes to a remote repository
Retrieve changes from a remote repository
questions.e: git pull downloads and merges changes from a remote repository.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a version control system (VCS) in software development?
o: Track changes in source code and collaborate on development
questions.e: A version control system tracks changes to source code and helps teams work together.

questions.q: Which software development methodology emphasizes continuous delivery and collaboration between cross-functional teams?
questions.e: DevOps joins development and operations with continuous delivery.

questions.q: What does the term "agile" refer to in software development?
o: A lightweight software development methodology emphasizing flexibility and collaboration
A system for managing network security
questions.e: Agile is a flexible, collaborative way of developing software in short cycles.

questions.q: Which type of software development methodology emphasizes iterative and incremental development?
questions.e: Agile develops iteratively and incrementally.

questions.q: What does the term "MVC" stand for in software architecture?
questions.e: MVC stands for Model View Controller.

questions.q: Which programming language is known for its high performance and is commonly used for building system-level software?
questions.e: C++ is fast and gives low-level control, so it is common for system software.
